messages.subject: Problem with Adobe Bridge updating Hierarchial Subject tag
messages.subject_clean: Problem with Adobe Bridge updating Hierarchial Subject tag
messages.body_plain:
Hello:

We have been using Adobe bridge to add tags to our photos.  However, we have just noticed that if we place an incorrect tag and then change it, it only changes it in the "subject" tag, not the "Hierarchical Subject" tag (which is what camtrapR is reading).  Instead, the Hierarchial Subject tag retains both the first tag and the corrected tag.  See my example below:

Subject                         : None, Species, Session, Summer2018, County, Cam ID, D3, Jeff Davis
History Action                  : saved, saved
History Instance ID             : xmp.iid:aeb6a04b-4b56-1441-963e-c390ce436bfe, xmp.iid:733a71e1-32a3-c945-8605-c0711859b34e
History When                    : 2018:12:05 18:36:31-06:00, 2019:01:22 00:52:20-06:00
History Software Agent          : Adobe Photoshop Camera Raw 10.1, Adobe Photoshop Camera Raw 11.0 (Windows)
History Changed                 : /metadata, /metadata
Hierarchical Subject            : Species|Pronghorn, Species|None, Species, Session, Session|Summer2018, County, County|Jeff davis, Cam ID, Cam ID|D3, County|Jeff Davis

You'll notice that Pronghorn is no longer in the subject tag and it does not show up in Adobe Bridge. (this is what we wanted).  But when you look at the Hierarchical Subject tag, it is still there and camtrapR uses it when creating the recordTable.

Have you experienced this problem and do you know how to get Bridge to update the tags in the Hierarchical Subject?  Or is there another workaround?

Thank you for your help.
Patricia

messages.subject_clean: Error in as.POSIXlt.character(x, tz, ...) : character string is not in a standard unambiguous format @spatialDetectionHistory
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ali,
the DateTimeOriginal column is a factor, not a date/time object. This means R doesn't know it is a date. It should be in POSIXct format.

The seconds are lost probably because you opened the table in Excel and saved it there. You can get the original (including seconds) back in POSIXct format by running:

recordTable.all.df$DateTimeOriginal <- as.POSIXct(paste(recordTable.all.df$Date, recordTable.all.df$Time), tz = "UTC")

Set argument tz to whatever the correct time zone is, with UTC being a reasonable default even if your cameras were in a different time zone (because UTC does not have daylight saving time, see the vignette for more details). If your time zone has daylight saving time, use UTC. Otherwise, go ahead and use the correct time zone. See this thread <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/camtrapr/ID1lZANf4P4> for more information.

To avoid all character columns being converted to factors try loading the record table with read.csv(..., stringsAsFactors = FALSE).

It is hard to say whether the camera operation matrix is correct. If it is all NA, then clearly no. If there are cells with numbers, it should be fine.

Best,
Jürgen
